meta.title: Quick Start — Autional Docs
meta.description: Run the full Autional identity platform locally in 3 steps. Clone, boot with Docker Compose, and sign in to the admin console.

index.title: Run the full Autional platform locally in 3 clear steps.
index.lead: This documentation hub helps new engineers go from local boot to system understanding quickly. Start the platform, validate the gateway, then move into the docs that match your task: architecture, APIs, security, or deployment.

steps.title: Clone and boot the platform
steps.body: Start the local stack so every service, gateway route, and operational dependency is available for exploration.
steps.command:
# Boot the full local stack (middleware + all 27 services); the first run takes about 2-3 minutes
docker compose -f docker-compose.infra.yml -f docker-compose.monolith.yml up -d

steps.title: Verify the gateway
steps.body: Check health first, then move into the interactive docs once the gateway is responding.

steps.title: Sign in to the admin console
steps.body: Sign in with the sample credentials (local demos only — do not use in production) to inspect tenants, auth flows, policies, and configuration from the UI.

meta.title: Architecture — Autional Docs
meta.description: Autional architecture overview — 27 Go microservices in a 4-tier design with cross-cutting security and observability.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.lead: Autional runs as 27 independently deployable Go microservices, organized in a 4-tier architecture with a cross-cutting layer.

rows.purpose: Zero-dependency foundation: errors, config loading, ID generation

tier3.title: Tier 3: Domain
tier3.middlewareBody: auth (JWT/IP whitelist), app bootstrap, gRPC factory, error handler, audit, tenant resolver
tier3.sharedBody: domain events (550+ event types), RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC, PIM, compliance, wallet, billing, notification

cross.title: Cross-Cutting
cross.lead: — ports, error codes, event names, table names, RBAC permissions. Every service depends on this layer.

meta.title: Auth Concepts — Autional Docs
meta.description: How authentication works in Autional — password hashing, token management, OIDC flows, session lifecycle, and multi-factor authentication.

authConcepts.title: Authentication Concepts
authConcepts.lead: How authentication works in Autional — from password hashing to OIDC flows.

modes.title: Password Transmission Modes
modes.lead: Autional supports 4 password transmission modes, configurable per tenant:

hashing.title: Password Hashing (Server-Side)
hashing.before: After transmission, passwords are hashed with
hashing.after: . The system also keeps bcrypt as a fallback for legacy data and supports per-tenant algorithm selection.

oauth.title: OAuth 2.1 / OIDC
oauth.lead: Autional implements the full OAuth 2.1 + OpenID Connect provider stack:
items: Token Exchange (RFC 8693) — NHI and AI agent authentication

saml.title: SAML 2.0
saml.body: Enterprise single sign-on (SSO) via SAML 2.0 IdP, with metadata exchange, SLO, and attribute mapping. Configured through the admin console.

meta.title: Security Guide — Autional Docs
meta.description: Security best practices for Autional in production — secret management, TLS, password policies, API key rotation, and audit logging.

security.title: Security Guide
security.lead: Security best practices for configuring Autional in production environments.

mfa.title: MFA Configuration
mfa.lead: Autional supports 5 MFA methods, configurable per tenant:

adaptive.title: Adaptive MFA (Risk Engine)
adaptive.lead: The adaptive MFA engine evaluates 10 signal categories to determine authentication risk:

items.label: IP risk
items.body: — risk scoring based on the source IP

items.label: Login failure rate
items.body: — detection of repeated failures within a short window

policy.title: Password Policy
items: Minimum/maximum length, complexity rules (upper, lower, digit, special)
Password history (the most recent N passwords cannot be reused)
Expiry (configurable days, forced reset on expiry)

encryption.title: Encryption at Rest
encryption.body: Field-level AES-256-GCM encryption with key rotation support; SM4-GCM for national cryptography compliance.

audit.title: Audit Trail
audit.body: All authentication events are recorded in an immutable Merkle hash chain audit log, with cryptographic verification for tamper-proof integrity.

meta.title: Multi-Tenancy — Autional Docs
meta.description: B2B SaaS multi-tenancy in Autional — per-tenant isolation, custom branding, domain verification, and tenant-aware RBAC.

multiTenant.title: Multi-Tenancy Guide
multiTenant.lead: Autional was built for B2B SaaS multi-tenancy from day one. Every feature is tenant-aware by design.

rows.name: 1. Schema
rows.enforcement: Every table has a tenant_id column

rows.name: 2. Repository
rows.enforcement: Every query includes a tenant_id WHERE clause

rows.name: 3. Handler
rows.enforcement: tenant_id is taken from the auth context, never from the request body

config.title: Tenant Configuration
config.lead: Each tenant can be configured independently:

items.label: Password policy
items.body: — min length, complexity, expiry, breach check

items.label: Branding
items.body: — custom login page, logo, colors, domain

members.title: Member Management
members.lead: Tenant members are managed through an invitation workflow:
members.body: Supports departmental hierarchy, delegated administration, and bulk imports (SCIM 2.0).

nhi.title: NHI (Non-Human Identity)
nhi.lead: AI agents, robots, and IoT devices are first-class identity citizens in Autional. Each NHI type has its own lifecycle state machine and authentication methods.

meta.title: Compliance — Autional Docs
meta.description: Compliance tools in Autional — control libraries and workflow tooling for 10 standards: ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, PSD2, PIPL, Dengbao 2.0, NIST SP 800-63B, and minor protection.

compliance.title: Compliance Tools
compliance.warning1: ⚠️ Autional is NOT certified for any compliance framework.

warning2.before: The tools described on this page help you
warning2.after: held by Autional. Achieving certification requires organization-specific policies, controls, and third-party audits. Do not rely on these tools alone for compliance.

compliance.lead: Autional includes built-in control libraries and workflow tooling for 10 compliance standards. These tools are designed to help your organization manage compliance processes — they are not certifications themselves.

rows.support: DSAR request management, 16-service erasure orchestration, consent audit trail (13 controls)
Annex A access control family (A.5.15–A.8.16) control register (10 controls)
CC6 logical and physical access common criteria controls (10 controls)
IAM-related controls and evidence management (14 controls)
Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) technical requirement controls (8 controls)
Notice-consent and related IAM provision controls (10 controls)
Identity authentication / access control / security audit controls (20 controls)
Authenticator and verifier requirement controls (AAL1–AAL3) (17 controls)
COPPA / PIPL minor protection / GDPR Art.8 / UK Code consolidated controls (12 controls)

hash.title: Hash-Chain Audit Logs
hash.body: Every authentication event is recorded in a Merkle hash chain. The integrity of the chain can be cryptographically verified, providing tamper-proof evidence for auditors.

retention.title: Data Retention
retention.body: Retention policies are configurable per data type, with scheduled archival and cleanup jobs; audit logs can be retained indefinitely.

classification.title: Data Classification
classification.body: Data classification and grading management: label sensitivity levels by data category, with level values customizable per organization.
